svg.title: macOS · Photo viewer / grading editor · Masks tab · found shape selected · 1000×700
svg.desc: Mirrors App/PhotoViewerView.swift (masksTab, controlRail; selectedShapeID, shapeTool, shapeSquareLock, selectedRegisterShapeIndex, registerShapeBinding, shapesEdited) hosting App/Overlay/OverlayMasksPanel.swift (shapesCard, shapeTile, RegisterShapeTile, shapeDetailCard, shapeCaption, shapeToolMenu) with App/Overlay/RegisterShapeOverlay.swift on the picture and LetsLapseKit/Shapes/ShapeRegister.swift (DetectedShape: kind, family, source, obliquity) behind the captions. Code first, mirrored from the running app 2026-09-11 (captures mac-masks-shape-selected.png, 1000×700, and mac-masks-shape-selected-tall.png, 1000×1000, for the whole detail card; 2×, window top at px 52). Same window, same project and picture as photo-viewer.masks.svg: the Masks tab with a REGISTER SHAPE selected — the "◎ Circle" tile the Find shapes pass found on the clock face — and no mask selected, so the deck shows no ring and the mask detail card is absent (a register selection and a deck selection are exclusive; choosing one clears the other). THE RAIL IS DRAWN SCROLLED BY 66 pt so that the Shapes card and the whole shape detail card sit inside the 1000×700 window (the capture at 700 clips the card after its hint; the 1000-tall capture supplies the rest): the pinned tab bar stays at y 60–96, the scroll viewport runs y 102–720, the creation toolbar (Linear · Radial · ＋ Shape · ＋ Custom…, see photo-viewer.masks.svg) has scrolled above it and is not drawn, the deck’s top 16 pt are clipped, and the Custom Masks card’s top edge just enters at the bottom. Unscrolled the cards sit at deck 152, Shapes 335, shape detail 608, Custom Masks 784. Content width 293 pt beside the 15 pt scroller gutter (thumb drawn). SHAPES CARD: "Shapes" 13/600 secondary + mono "5 shapes"; a 3-column grid (8 pt columns, 10 pt rows) of RegisterShapeTile — LL.ink 4:3 tiles (83×62.25, radius 7) with the picture’s 3:4 frame letterboxed inside (46 pt wide, 0.5 pt white-25% hairline) and the shape filled white-90% at its place; the selected tile carries a 2 pt accent strokeBorder (inside the tile). Captions "◎ Square" · "◎ Square" · "◎ Rectangle" / "◎ Circle" · "✎ Square": the 9 pt glyph is the source (◎ detected by Find shapes, ✎ drawn here with ＋ Shape), the 11/600 name the family — Circle when obliquity (minor ÷ major) ≥ 0.85, else Oval; Square when the quad’s sides are within tolerance, else Rectangle — or the user’s own name. Legend in two lines. SHAPE DETAIL CARD (shapeDetailCard, 14 pt padding, 12 pt rows): a 30×24 RegisterShapeTile thumbnail (no ring), the "Shape name" TextField — plain style, 14/700, showing its PLACEHOLDER because this found shape has no name yet; typing one names it (the caption and the tile then use it; Return commits) — and Remove 12/600 secondary, which drops the shape from the register; the caption 11.5 pt secondary "Circle · found by Find shapes · 1350 px across · 93% round" (family · origin · major axis in NATIVE pixels of the register’s frame · obliquity as a percentage; wraps after the last dot at this width); the hint 11 pt secondary "Drag the centre to move it, the axis handles to size it, the stalk to turn it." (wrapping after "to"); and the bordered "◌ Use as Radial mask" button (macOS .bordered: 22 pt white, radius 6, hairline + soft shadow, circle.dashed + 12.5/600 label) which copies the ellipse into the deck as a Radial mask — the deck’s "Circle" in photo-viewer.masks.svg is exactly that copy, which is why both files draw the same ellipse. QUAD VARIANT (desc-only): a Rectangle / Square tile selected shows four corner handles plus the centre on the picture; the card gains a "Square lock" checkbox (13.5/600) under the caption with its own footnote — on: "Corner drags scale the whole shape, so a square stays square."; off: "Each corner moves on its own — a rectangle, or a quad seen at an angle." — and the caption reads "Square · drawn here · 812×812 px"-style width×height; where the button would be, the tertiary line "Rectangle masks come later." PICTURE CHROME (RegisterShapeOverlay, ellipse; every coordinate in picture points, top-left origin — the 3:4 still is 504×672 at x 98, native 3024×4032, so 1 pt = 6 px): centre (372.5, 409), semi-axes 112.5 × 104.5 (1350 × 1255 px), rotation −10°. The outline is stroked twice — 1.4 pt white, then LL.amber-90% 1.2 pt dashed 5/4; the two axes are ticked white-50% 1 pt dashed 3/3 from end to end; the CENTRE HANDLE is a 22 pt amber disc with a 1.5 pt white strokeBorder and a 9 pt bold white arrow.up.and.down.and.arrow.left.and.right (drag = move; a rectangle’s corners move with it); the two AXIS HANDLES are 13.2 pt white squares (radius 3, amber 1.5 pt border) at the +major (east) and −minor (north) ends — the east one sets majorAxis, the north one minorAxis, each clamped to ≥ 4 pt; the ROTATION STALK is a 1 pt white-70% line from the east handle to a knob at major + 34 pt — a 22 pt disc of black-35% with the white border and a white arrow.clockwise; dragging it sets rotation from the pointer’s angle about the centre. While a handle is down the HUD reads "Circle · 1350 px across · −10°" (a quad: "Square · 812×812 px"); on release the shape is re-measured in the native frame and the register saved. Handles take a drag before the armed-tool gesture. Hooks: LL_EDITOR=<uuid|latest>, LL_RAIL=masks, LL_SHAPETOOL=ellipse|rect|square (arms ＋ Shape at launch); the selection itself is a click on the tile. Verified against the running Mac app 2026-09-11.
